paper_title: A Simple Algorithmic Framework for Disambiguation of Finite Automata
statement: Similarly to [33], the previous result provides sufficient conditions for termination when disambiguating WFA for each level of ambiguity. We leave as an open problem to understand when the R-twins property is a necessary condition in each case.
context: ▶ Theorem 9. Let W be a WFA over T and R ∈ {CFW , ICFW , ECFW }. If W satisfies the R-twins property, then WF is finite when F = (ΠOR , facM , resM ) is a PF-oracle. Similarly to [33], the previous result provides sufficient conditions for termination when disambiguating WFA for each level of ambiguity. We leave as an open problem to understand when the R-twins property is a necessary condition in each case. 6 Future work As an initial paper on this algorithmic framework, numerous approaches remain to be explored for further study. Besides the open problems we have stated throughout the paper, some natural follow-up work would be extending the framework onto tree automata [15], cost-register automata [4], or Büchi automata [43]. In the last case, it is an open problem to find good disambiguation algorithms, since deterministic Büchi automata are less expressive than unambiguous ones. It will be interesting to see if the algorithmic framework presented here could lead to new insights on the disambiguation of Büchi automata. We highlight one open problem, posed in Section 4, we find particularly interesting, which is to find optimal disambiguation schemes that minimize the number of explored states. Finally, our disambiguation framework is simple enough to be implemented and used in practice. We are interested in seeing it being explored as an alternative to determinization in real-life cases where an unambiguous, or a boundedly ambiguous automaton, is good enough.
